ns2:section.sectionText: Topic Section T: Remade in America: International Films in American Hands This section of English 300 is designed to offer students interested in film a chance to investigate the commercial and artistic roles that foreign films play in the U.S. filmscape. In addition to studying, applying, and refining the formal elements of the various genres of writing about film (reviews, analytical essays, production histories), we will examine the sorts of challenges that foreign films pose for spectators and for filmmakers. Viewing and discussing films from a range of national traditions and periods and then studying their American remakes will also help us to understand the values and practices of Hollywood?s corporate culture. Evaluated work will include four projects amounting to 25?30 pages of formal writing, some of which will involve oral presentations. While helpful, previous experience in film analysis is not essential. It is strongly recommended that all English and Teaching of English majors take ENGL 300 and ENGL 301 BEFORE taking any other 300- or 400-level courses. ENGL 300 is restricted to English/Rhetoric Majors Some seats are available to non-English majors.
